name: Dojikko (clumsy girl)
blurb: The lovable klutz who trips on flat ground, drops trays and bounces back smiling
title: Dojikko: Clumsy Girl Trope Meaning, Poses & Drawing Reference
description: Dojikko meaning and reference: the clumsy character who trips on flat ground, classic clumsy moments, and how to draw and safely stage falling poses.
answer: Dojikko is the Japanese name for a clumsy character, from doji, a blunder, plus ko, child. The dojikko trips over nothing, drops what she carries and gets tangled in her own feet, yet keeps trying, and that persistence is what makes the trope endearing.

body: Doji means a careless slip-up, and a dojikko is someone who makes them constantly. The signature gag, tripping on flat ground, is so common in anime that it became a shorthand for the type. Dojikko characters are often maids, new employees or first-day transfer students, roles where carrying trays, papers and boxes gives plenty of things to drop.
The trope works because the clumsiness is never mean-spirited. The character is sincere and hard-working, the mistakes are harmless, and a quick apology or embarrassed laugh follows each one.

sections.h: How to draw a trip or fall
body: Sell the motion with the line of action: a long diagonal from the trailing foot to the outstretched hands. The leading foot should catch behind something, or behind nothing, while the body pitches forward past its base of balance.

Scatter the carried objects along the arc of the fall, smaller and higher the earlier they left the hands. For the aftermath, the seated landing with legs folded to one side, one hand rubbing the head and an embarrassed grin, is the most recognisable single image. Spiral eyes or a small star over the head add comedy.

Never have a model actually fall. Fake the moment: a mid-stumble pose held on one foot with a hand on a wall out of frame, or start from the floor and shoot the landing. Paper or light props tossed by an assistant read as the spill.
Use a fast shutter for flying props and a slightly low camera to make the stumble look larger. A soft floor, a clear space and short takes keep everyone safe.

faq.a: A clumsy, accident-prone character; doji means a blunder and ko means child.

faq.q: Why do anime characters trip on flat ground?
faq.a: It is the classic dojikko gag: tripping on nothing shows the character's clumsiness at its purest and sets up a cute recovery.

faq.q: How do I photograph a falling pose safely?
faq.a: Fake it: hold a supported mid-stumble pose or shoot the landing from the floor, and throw light props for motion instead of falling.
